purpose: Fixed axes and vocabulary for docs/execution_matrix.json: every model that Titanos records ever tried, against every platform slot, with one consistent cell state. Untried and not-applicable cells are explicit so gaps can be built toward.

pass.meaning: executed on this slot with the intended modality output verified by a recorded receipt (evidence id required)

fail.meaning: executed on this slot and failed or produced unacceptable output; the failure is retained (evidence id required)

partial.meaning: executed a narrower gate on this slot: load-only, prepared graph or operator subset, CPU fallback, quality-limited or bounded fixture (evidence id required; note says which gate)

untried.meaning: not executed on this slot with matrix-cited evidence; the note names one of three kinds: `untried: runnable by construction` (the backend has an execution path through an available runtime on the slot, named in the note, and the identity names an acquirable artifact; the artifact may be present or still to be acquired, nothing is claimed about the outcome, and whether a fleet host covers the slot is a host circumstance recorded in named_devices and no_fleet_host, never part of the claim), `untried: no fleet host for slot` (runnable by construction, but no host in the fleet covers the slot today: no_fleet_host, a host circumstance and never a construction na) or `untried: execution recorded by a reader but no evidence id the capability matrix cites` (evidence binding pending)

na.meaning: not applicable (reason required in the note): a reader recorded Titanos refusing the configuration by design, or the cell cannot exist by construction: the row backend has no execution path on the slot runtimes (backend_runtime_map; a converted artifact is its own row), a runtime the backend needs publishes no package for the slot platform (runtime_availability), the row identity names no acquirable artifact (unrecorded_identity_rule; recorded executions stand), the row names a model variant Titanos's runner rejects before load (unsupported_variant_rule); for multi-GPU mode cells also Titanos's own refusal of the mode for the backend/task (multi_gpu_modes_rule.admission), the refusal shared from the pair's single/replicas receipts, or a slot that cannot form the GPU group or declare the explicit CPU/XPU group through a runtime available for the row's backend. A slot with no fleet host is never na (no_fleet_host is an untried kind)

backend_runtime_map.rule: a row's catalog backend has an execution path on a slot only when at least one token in the slot's `runtimes` list is in the backend's list below and is available on the slot (runtime_availability). The entry `cpu` stands for the matrix kit's `cpu` runtime: on a slot that lists any token in `cpu_tokens`, the backend's CPU path runs through its own `cpu_path_tokens`, the runtimes the backend imports, and exists only when every one of those is available on the slot (the per-slot lists understate CPU runtimes, so a CPU slot grants every CPU-capable backend its own CPU path unless runtime_availability removes a token it needs; onnx-diffusers needs onnxruntime and torch: src/titanos/onnx_images.py:123 imports diffusers OnnxStableDiffusionPipeline/OnnxRuntimeModel/PNDMScheduler, :193 reports 'Torch CPU PNDM scheduling', and pyproject.toml:24 dml-vision pins torch>=2.8,<2.9, so its CPU path needs `onnx CPU` and `diffusers CPU` together). A cell whose backend has no path on the slot cannot exist by construction and is `na` with the reason; a converted artifact (an ONNX or OpenVINO export, a GGUF) is its own catalog row, never a path for the source row. The builder's untried note names the granting tokens (the slot's available tokens that are in the backend's list, plus all of the backend's cpu_path_tokens when the cpu rule applies and every one is available), never the slot's raw runtime list

backend_runtime_map.kit_runtimes_rule: tools/matrix_kit/slots.py runtime name -> the slot runtime tokens it stands for (`cpu` is the map entry `cpu`, which cpu_tokens expand). tests/check_matrix_kit.py asserts that for every backend and every kit runtime, membership in run_cells.py COMPAT[runtime] equals holding one of these tokens in the backend's list; a slot token in no kit runtime is listed in tokens_without_kit_runtime with the reason, and every slot token must be a cpu token, a kit-runtime token or listed there 2026-09-25: `native-sycl` added: tools/matrix_kit/slots.py probe_native_sycl runs the catalogued SYCL llama.cpp build's --list-devices (given with run_cells.py --native-sycl) and maps its Intel GPUs to the Intel GPU slots as device native:SYCLn, the address Titanos's native runner verifies against the same inventory (src/titanos/native.py:96-111); COMPAT['native-sycl'] holds llama-cpp only. `llama.cpp SYCL` therefore left tokens_without_kit_runtime (its former entry: "the kit probes no llama.cpp native device; the path is Titanos's catalogued win-sycl-x64 / ubuntu-sycl-fp16-x64 / ubuntu-sycl-fp32-x64 native profiles on the Intel GPU slots (native_llama_cpp_profiles), executed by no run yet, so the builder fills those cells as untried").

native_llama_cpp_profiles.rule: One rule for every native llama.cpp profile Titanos catalogs (src/titanos/data/native-profiles.json, release b10809; all source_only per docs/ROSTER.md:59): a profile is a declared llama-cpp execution path on the matrix slots whose OS and architecture it is built for and whose accelerator its flavor targets (src/titanos/runtime_catalog.py:58-60 flavors: CPU, CUDA, Vulkan, OpenVINO, ROCm, SYCL, OpenCL), through the token named in `mapped`; Titanos offers a profile on any host whose os/arch match (runtime_catalog.py:55; 'Explicit runtime choice; device support is verified when loading', :62) and places a non-CUDA device as native:<name> from llama-server --list-devices (src/titanos/native.py:96-111, one device per replica; src/titanos/config.py:152-153). A declared path no run has executed is `untried`, never na (the standard already applied to `torch XPU` on the Windows Intel slots and `llama.cpp OpenCL` on the Adreno slot). A profile built for an accelerator API the matrix defines no slot around is listed in `unmapped` with the reason: mapping it would widen a slot defined by another API or add a slot, a slot-axis decision for the owner, not a rule the builder applies. Slot tokens that predate this rule and rest on Titanos's own packages rather than this catalog (`llama.cpp CUDA` on linux-x64-nvidia-cuda, `llama.cpp CUDA aarch64`) are outside it. tests/check_execution_matrix.py asserts every catalogued profile appears exactly once in mapped or unmapped, every mapped token is in backends.llama-cpp or is the cpu token, and every mapped slot has the profile's platform and lists the token

unrecorded_identity_rule.rule: a row is identity-unrecorded only when its catalog identity text both matches trigger_regex and names no acquirable artifact at all: no repository slug (owner/name; Titanos tree paths and document references such as docs/X.md are excluded by slug_exclude, as are version-like owners), no URL, no local filesystem path and no content digest. A row that names any of those (for example wan2.1-t2v-1.3b: repository slug plus a local D: path; tiny-random-bert-export-fixture: repository slug, revision f171d7ba in the E-001 note) is acquirable and its cells stay untried or reader-provided. A reader-recorded execution (pass, fail, partial) always stands; the na reason names it

unsupported_variant_rule.rule: a row whose catalog identity names a model variant that the row's Titanos runner rejects before load is not applicable by construction on every slot: the refusal is a code fact of the checked-in tree (cited per variant), the same standard the multi_gpu_modes_rule applies to Titanos's mode refusals; it needs no receipt because no runtime, device or weight is consulted before the rejection. The family's supported variant is untouched by this rule and stays untried until executed. A reader-recorded execution of such a row would contradict the citation and always stands (the builder ranks it above na), which is the signal to fix the rule

no_fleet_host.rule: a slot with no host in the fleet is a host circumstance, not a fact about the platform, the catalog identity or Titanos's own code, so it is never a construction na. A cell on such a slot that is otherwise runnable by construction (backend path through an available runtime, acquirable identity) is `untried: no fleet host for slot <slot> (since <date>)` with the reason below; a cell that is na by identity or by backend path is na for that reason as on any other slot; a reader-recorded state always wins. tests/check_execution_matrix.py enforces that no na note cites a missing fleet host and that every no-fleet-host untried cell is on a listed slot and runnable by construction

runtime_availability.rule: a slot runtime token gives a backend an execution path only when the package behind it is published for the slot platform under Titanos's pyproject pins (available). An entry below with available=false removes that token from the slot in the builder's has_path and, through backend_runtime_map.cpu_path_tokens, removes the CPU path of every backend any of whose cpu_path_tokens is unavailable on the slot (the CPU path needs every runtime the backend imports). These are facts about published wheels for a platform (true by construction for the platform), never about what a host has installed: the matrix kit records what is installed in HOST_DETECTION.json and needs no change. A reader-recorded pass, fail or partial on the slot always stands, and tests/check_execution_matrix.py reports any executed cell an entry here would contradict instead of accepting the entry (a kit fail that is only an import or install error is not an execution: the kit files such cells as untried when its host probe finds the runtime absent, tools/matrix_kit/run_cells.py missing_runtime_cell). The explicit CPU/XPU tensor-parallel group of multi_gpu_modes_rule likewise exists only through an available token for the row's backend
runtime_availability.source: PyPI JSON API https://pypi.org/pypi/<package>/<version>/json and https://pypi.org/pypi/torch/json (release file lists); measured 2026-09-25 and re-verified the same day from this workstation (urllib; the per-version file counts recorded below are what the re-verification saw); re-verified again with the same method (workstation date 2026-09-24; identical file counts and platform tags for torch 2.8.0, 2.9.0, 2.9.1, 2.10.0, 2.11.0, 2.12.0, 2.12.1, 2.2.2 and 2.3.0, openvino 2026.3.1, openvino-genai 2026.3.1.0, onnxruntime 1.27.0 and 1.23.2; PyPI lists exactly those seven torch releases in [2.8, 2.13)); re-verified a third time on 2026-09-25 (same method, same file counts; the per-platform wheel counts in `packages` are from that run, which also counted win_arm64: 0 for every torch release in range, 0 for openvino and openvino-genai, 4 for onnxruntime 1.27.0). download.pytorch.org (Titanos's tools/profiles.json index for torch) was not queried; its profiles declare their platforms explicitly and are cited where they decide 2026-09-25 (wave D): the win-arm64-cpu torch entries were converted to deviations after the snapdragon-x-laptop-win-arm64 receipts executed torch 2.9.1+cpu (cp312-cp312-win_arm64 from download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu): the PyPI counts were right and incomplete; download.pytorch.org publishes win_arm64 CPU wheels

platform_tags.rule: the wheel platform family a slot's platform installs from (platform_slots os/arch -> family); a token's package is `available` on a slot only when the family is in the package's published_platforms; tests/check_execution_matrix.py derives from these tables that every token in token_packages on a slot (the slot's runtimes plus, on a CPU slot, every cpu token) whose package publishes no wheel for the slot family is either declared unavailable in `slots` or carries an executed-deviation exception in `deviations`, and that every declared-unavailable entry agrees with the package table

token_packages.rule: runtime token -> the measured package it installs; tokens absent here are not wheel-checked: llama.cpp tokens are Titanos's catalogued native binaries (native_llama_cpp_profiles), tesseract is a host binary, sherpa-onnx (sherpa-onnx==1.13.8) and the DirectML/QNN/Core ML/VitisAI ONNX providers (onnxruntime-directml, onnxruntime-windowsml, onnxruntime-qnn) were not measured

admission.rule: Titanos's own admission of the matrix kit's multi-GPU modes (the kit sets ModelSpec.parallelism = mode and WorkerSpec.mode = mode, docs/MATRIX_KIT.md). A mode is admitted for a row only when: the backend is not a one-device backend; the task is not a single-device task (single_device_tasks, each cited to its refusing line in single_device_task_lines); for tensor_parallel the backend and task are in the tensor_parallel lists; for model_sharding the backend is in the model_sharding list. A mode Titanos refuses by design is na for the row on every slot (never 'untried: runnable by construction'); an admitted mode is then judged by the slot's group rule (modes below). When a (model, slot) pair's receipt-backed cells (single, replicas) are all na by refusal, its builder-filled multi-GPU cells are na with the same refusal
admission.source: src/titanos/config.py, read 2026-09-25: ModelSpec validator 80-82 (ace-step refuses parallelism other than single), 97-100 (sherpa-onnx), 117-118 (image-segmentation), 150-151 (llama-cpp: 'Use native options for llama-cpp placement'; llama.cpp's own native split modes take device=native:... with native.split_mode and are not a matrix mode), 74-77 (diarization: the validator calls src/titanos/diarization.py prepare, whose lines 33-38 refuse any parallelism other than single: 'Diarization requires a reviewed local Sherpa ONNX bundle on one CPU'), 170-172 (vad: 'VAD requires the single-device CPU ONNX adapter'), 190-191 (onnx, openvino, openvino-genai: 'Compiled model sharding is not implemented'), 211-212 (translation, image-to-text, object-detection, sentiment, rerank, pair-classification, depth-estimation: 'API Plus adapters currently use one device per worker'), 233-234 (tensor_parallel requires backend transformers and task in {chat, vision, embeddings}), 237-238 (xtts and qwen3-tts: 'This speech backend uses one device per worker'); onnx_images.py:19 (onnx-diffusers) and tesseract.py:57 (tesseract) refuse parallelism other than single; Config validator 334-335 (diarization: worker.mode other than single refused, 'Diarization replicas require one CPU worker'), 336-337 (translation, image-to-text, object-detection, sentiment, rerank, depth-estimation, image-segmentation, music: 'API Plus adapters require single-device workers'), 345-346 ('This model adapter does not implement tensor parallelism' unless transformers chat/vision/embeddings), 347-348 ('Model sharding requires Transformers or Diffusers'); WorkerSpec validator 272-275 (tensor_parallel needs two assigned GPUs or an explicit CPU/XPU group; model_sharding needs at least two assigned GPUs)
admission.added: 2026-09-25 (round 4): diarization and vad added (round-3 review finding 5); harmless for today's sherpa-onnx and onnx rows, which mode_refusal already refuses by backend, but a future transformers diarization row must not be filed 'untried: runnable by construction' for model_sharding

model_sharding.reason: model sharding requires at least two assigned GPUs (src/titanos/config.py WorkerSpec); a slot whose runtimes cannot form a homogeneous CUDA or ROCm GPU group (tools/matrix_kit/slots.py forms groups only from torch CUDA/ROCm devices) has no such group by construction

tensor_parallel.reason: tensor parallel needs two assigned GPUs or an explicit CPU Gloo / XPU XCCL rank group (docs/MULTIGPU.md); a groupless slot other than a CPU or XPU slot has no such group by construction, while the explicit CPU/XPU group is a runnable configuration the matrix kit has not run, so those cells stay untried; the explicit group exists only through a runtime available on the slot for the row's backend (an available cpu_path_token for `cpu`, or `torch XPU` not removed by runtime_availability), so a transformers row on macos-x64, where no torch wheel exists, would get na by construction, not untried

multi_gpu_modes_rule.applies_to: mode_cells pairs (model, slot) that have a receipt for some mode but none for a multi-GPU mode; a receipt-backed state always wins; the kit (tools/matrix_kit/run_cells.py missing_group_cell, mode_refusal) applies the same admission and group rules when it has no group to run; the builder's mode_gap_reason(row, slot, mode) and the test's slot_forms_group(row, slot, mode) take the row because the explicit CPU group depends on the backend's available cpu_path_tokens

row_identity_rule: one row per individual model: repository@revision (full or 7+ hex), or content sha256, or a named release asset; combined roster rows (fixture sets, historical sets) are split into their members; task and backend are separate columns, never folded into the name
evidence_rule: pass/fail/partial cells cite E-ids that exist in docs/CAPABILITY_MATRIX.md and, where available, a receipt path; a cell may not be pass unless the cited receipt records execution of that model on that slot (OS, arch, accelerator)
